title: Scalar-p torus isogenies are relative Frobenius up to isomorphism
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] of characteristic $p>0$. Let $G$ be a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Here unipotent means that all geometric points act by unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq G$: a subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ and maximal among tori, where $\mathbf G_m(R)=R^\times$. Write $X^*(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{F\text{-groups}}(T,\mathbf G_m)$. Let $f:G\to G$ be a surjective $F$-group-scheme homomorphism with finite scheme-theoretic kernel, where finite means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra. Assume $f(T)\subseteq T$ as a factorization of scheme morphisms, and
$$\chi\circ f|_T=p\chi\qquad(\chi\in X^*(T)).$$
Put $C=F[G]$ and define the Frobenius twist $G^{(p)}=\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_{F,a\mapsto a^p}F)$ with its base-changed group law [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Define the relative Frobenius $F_{G/F}:G\to G^{(p)}$ by the coordinate-algebra homomorphism $b\otimes c\mapsto c b^p$. Then there exists an isomorphism of $F$-group schemes $h:G^{(p)}\xrightarrow{\sim}G$ such that $f=h\circ F_{G/F}$. No choice of a model over a finite field, compatibility with a chosen Borel, or prime-to-$p$ condition on the kernel is assumed. The cases of a torus and the trivial group are included.

source.place: Sections 2.25--2.29, printed pp.47--49 (relative Frobenius), and full isogeny theorem 23.25, printed pp.492--493 (existence and uniqueness up to an inner torus automorphism); isomorphism theorem 23.26. Scalar p isogeny specialization: compare f with relative Frobenius after the root-datum isomorphism between G^(p) and G, and absorb the inner torus automorphism into h.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-frobenius-twist] to $(G,T)$. It supplies the split reductive pair $(G^{(p)},T^{(p)})$, the full root-datum identification $\iota:X^*(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}X^*(T^{(p)})$, and the Frobenius isogeny $F_{G/F}$ with $(F_{G/F}|_T)^*\iota=p\,\mathrm{id}$. This is exactly the coordinate morphism specified in the statement, not a chosen finite-field model.

Use [lem-sfb-root-datum-isogeny-realization] with $(G_1,S_1)=(G^{(p)},T^{(p)})$, $(G_0,S_0)=(G,T)$ and $u=\iota$. The cokernel is zero. For each source root $\alpha^{(p)}$ choose $b(\alpha^{(p)})=\alpha$ and $q_{\alpha^{(p)}}=1$. The root equation is $\iota(\alpha)=\alpha^{(p)}$; the coroot equation is $\iota^\vee((\alpha^\vee)^{(p)})=\alpha^\vee$, supplied by step 1's full root-datum identification. Thus the cited existence theorem gives $g:G^{(p)}\to G$ inducing $\iota$ on characters, and its isomorphism criterion makes $g$ an isomorphism. No kernel separability hypothesis is required.

Set $a=g\circ F_{G/F}$ and $b=f$. The former is an isogeny because composition with an isomorphism preserves surjectivity and the kernel; the latter is one by hypothesis. Both map $T$ into $T$. For every character $\chi$, $\chi\circ a|_T=(\iota\chi)\circ F_{G/F}|_T=p\chi=\chi\circ f|_T$. Apply [lem-sfb-isogeny-torus-conjugacy] to these two maps with $G_1=G_0=G$ and $T_1=T_0=T$. It gives $t\in T(F)$ with $f=\operatorname{Int}(t)\circ g\circ F_{G/F}$.

source.place: Proposition 23.7, p.486; full isogeny theorem 23.25, pp.492--493.

proof.text: Define $h=\operatorname{Int}(t)\circ g$. Conjugation by $t^{-1}$ is inverse to conjugation by $t$, so $h$ is an isomorphism with inverse $g^{-1}\circ\operatorname{Int}(t^{-1})$. Step 3 gives $f=h\circ F_{G/F}$. When the roots are empty the same argument uses empty root bijections; for the trivial group both lattices are zero. Thus no rank, Borel compatibility or kernel reducedness assumption has been introduced.

source.place: 23.25--23.26, p.493; elementary composition of the obtained isomorphisms.

Sources read in Milne iAG2017: 2.27-2.29 (Prop 2.29: F_G is an isogeny of degree p^dim and faithfully flat), Prop 23.7 (p.486), Thm 23.25, Rem 23.26 and Cor 23.27 (pp.492-493). Step 1: the twist node's statement gives everything the step uses (G^(p) reductive, T^(p) split maximal, iota preserving roots/coroots/pairing, F_{G/F} an isogeny with T->T^(p), chi^(p)∘F|_T = p chi). Step 2: in lem-sfb-root-datum-isogeny-realization, u=iota is injective with zero cokernel; with b(alpha^(p))=alpha and q=1 the root equation iota(alpha)=alpha^(p) holds, and the coroot equation (alpha^vee)^(p)∘iota = alpha^vee holds because the pairing is preserved. Its existence clause gives g, and its isomorphism criterion (all q=1, u bijective) makes g an isomorphism. Step 3: a=g∘F has kernel ker F and is surjective; chi∘g∘F|_T = (iota chi)∘F|_T = p chi = chi∘f|_T, so the conjugacy node applies with G_1=G_0=G and gives f=Int(t)∘a. Step 4 is elementary. Twist node: true by 2.29 plus 23.27 base change along the automorphism sigma of the perfect field F; naturality gives the character formula, and the coordinate map is well defined. Torus-conjugacy node: Milne 23.7 over an algebraically closed F. The hypotheses force a(T_1)=T_0 and the same root-data isogeny. t exists in T_0(F) because the simple roots are independent and F^x is divisible. The order inn(t)∘phi_1 is the correct one; Milne's printed last line reverses it. Small cases checked: tori (a=b), trivial group, SL_2 in char 2 with non-reduced kernel, char 0. lean.statement: theorem scalarPIsogeny_relativeFrobenius {F : Type u} [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP F p] (G T : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) (i : T ⟶ G) (hG : ReductiveTorusCentralizer.IsReductive G) (hT : ReductiveTorusCentralizer.IsMaximalTorus i) (hsplit : ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (T ≅ MultiplicativeType.splitTorus F r)) (f : G ⟶ G) [Surjective f.hom.hom.left] [IsFinite (GrpObj.ker f.hom.hom).hom] (fT : T ⟶ T) (hfT : fT ≫ i = i ≫ f) (hscalar : ∀ χ : T.X ⟶ StandardGroupSchemes.multiplicative F, IsMonHom χ → fT.hom.hom ≫ χ = χ ^ p) : ∃ h : ((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (frobenius F p)))).mapGrp.obj G) ≅ G, ((f ≫ h.inv).hom.hom.left ≫ pullback.fst G.X.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (frobenius F p)))).IsFrobenius p
lean.note: The twist is (Over.pullback (Spec.map (frobenius F p))).mapGrp.obj G with its actual base-changed group law. The factorization is expressed equivalently by requiring f followed by h inverse and the projection to G to be absolute Frobenius. Both f and h lie over F, so the other projection is the structure map, and the pullback universal property gives exactly the relative Frobenius with coordinate map b tensor c ↦ c*b^p. IsFrobenius is nonvacuous here: the affine F-scheme G is of characteristic p.

IsReductive and IsMaximalTorus match the node over an algebraically closed F; hsplit allows rank 0. Surjectivity is on the underlying scheme; IsFinite applies to the scheme-theoretic GrpObj.ker, so non-reduced kernels are allowed. fT/hfT is the factorization of f through T. hscalar covers every IsMonHom character, and chi^p is Mathlib's pointwise Hom.monoid, i.e. p*chi. The twist is Over.pullback(Spec Frob).mapGrp, giving the base-changed group law.
